summary.headline: Oriental Aromatics posted record Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs 318.2 crore (+17% YoY) and PAT of Rs 5.70 crore, with consolidated EBITDA margin at 7.94%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 delivered the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue, up about 17% YoY and 22% QoQ, with operating EBITDA margin expanding 158 bps YoY to 7.94%. H1 consolidated revenue was about Rs 578 crore (+16.3% YoY), EBITDA Rs 45.07 crore and PAT Rs 8.3 crore versus Rs 1.2 crore. Camphor volumes fell YoY on alpha-pinene-driven price increases, while Mahad is ramping from a low base but still drags consolidated profit. Management announced a technical, strategic and manufacturing arrangement with Unilever Industries Private Limited but gave few details.

segments.name: Fragrances and Flavors
segments.commentary: Ambernath production rose 14% QoQ and sales volume rose 20% QoQ in Q2. Management cites FMCG home care and beauty volume growth and its internalisation of aroma ingredients as drivers.

segments.name: Specialty Aroma Ingredients (Baroda)
segments.commentary: Production rose 8% QoQ and sales volume rose 12% QoQ and 8% YoY in Q2; H1 sales volume up 10% YoY. Pricing pressure from Asian capacity additions and elevated, volatile terpene and petrochemical raw material costs persist.

segments.name: Camphor and Terpene Chemicals (Bareilly)
segments.commentary: Production rose 4% QoQ, but sales volume fell 5% QoQ and 8% YoY in Q2 after alpha-pinene price spike lifted camphor prices and hit pooja-segment offtake. H1 sales volume still up 11% YoY.

segments.name: Mahad (Specialty Aroma, new facility)
segments.commentary: Production rose 51% QoQ and sales volume rose 74% QoQ in Q2; Q2 revenue about Rs 4 crore per analyst question, which management did not dispute. Utilisation is about 50-55% of installed capacity and it remains a drag on consolidated profitability.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated long-term guidance of 10-12% sales growth (CAGR) and a first target of 10% EBITDA margin.
Full-year FY27 guidance, as confirmed on the call: about Rs 50 crore net profit on about Rs 1,000 crore turnover.
Mahad expected to reach optimum utilisation in two to three quarters, taking utilisation to at least 80%, after which pricing and contribution can improve.
Management expects RFQs won in June to go live from July and lift volumes in Q3 FY27.
Management said it will announce capex plans (brownfield or greenfield) in coming quarters; no timelines given.
capex_capacity: Mahad at about 50-55% of installed capacity; target is 80% or more within two to three quarters.
Company is in a consolidation phase with no substantial capex in the last one to one-and-a-half years; capex plans to be disclosed in coming quarters.
Mahad infrastructure designed to accommodate additional molecules and future expansion phases.
Management said R&D pipeline is being strengthened for new molecules and fragrance creation.
demand_pricing: Management said Indian FMCG volumes improved in Q2, with leading peers reporting double-digit volume growth in home care and beauty and well-being.
Specialty aroma ingredients face pricing pressure from Asian capacity additions; raw material inflation is hard to pass through given competition.
Camphor faces structural domestic overcapacity; alpha-pinene-driven price rises cut pooja-segment offtake, and management said retail pricing is below full pass-through level.
Management said the Q2 Camphor sales decline versus last year was driven by higher prices and high price sensitivity, not only by imports.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Unilever arrangement a CDMO/CMO tie-up, will it contribute to top line, and does it involve investment or advances?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share more than the exchange filing, calling it a work in progress, and gave no timelines.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Mahad revenue run-rate and will it reach EBITDA break-even this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said optimum volume utilisation is two to three quarters away, with pricing gains to follow; it did not answer the break-even question directly.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company deliver a 12% top-line CAGR and a 10% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 10-12% steady growth guidance and a 10% EBITDA target, attributing the gap to excess capacity and raw material inflation.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans for the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is in consolidation, evaluating multiple products, and will announce capex plans in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net debt-to-equity rise from 0.56 to 0.64 QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher inventory, receivables from late-quarter sales, and higher prices paid for inventory increased working capital use.

qa_highlights.question: Is revenue mix shifting toward fragrances, and what is the H2 pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited growth in fragrances from internalisation and long-term pricing; it reiterated a one-third each split across the three divisions.

risks_watch: Mahad utilisation must rise from about 50-55% toward 80%+ to cut the consolidated margin gap versus standalone (8.6% vs 7.8%).
Raw material inflation (alpha-pinene, terpene and petrochemical feedstocks) and limited pass-through to customers.
Camphor demand sensitivity in the pooja segment and domestic overcapacity; sales volumes fell YoY in Q2.
Net debt-to-equity rose to 0.64 from 0.56, driven by working capital.
Capex plans and Unilever arrangement economics remain undisclosed, with no timelines.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic on the numbers, citing record revenue and margin gains, but guarded on pricing, raw material costs and Mahad timelines. Management was evasive on the Unilever deal, capex and Mahad break-even, and gave no quantified timelines.
key_quotes: Our focus is now to convert this operational momentum into sustained improvements in profitability, capital efficiency, and long-term shareholder value through discipline and execution over the coming quarters.
So, we will, in the coming quarters, inform the investor community about what our CAPEX plans are.

growth.why: Management reiterated 10-12% sales CAGR and FY27 guidance of Rs 1,000 crore turnover and Rs 50 crore PAT, backed by Mahad ramping from about 52.5% utilisation to 80%+ within two to three quarters and RFQs won in June going live from July, though no new capacity has a timeline and capex plans are unspecified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 7.94% in Q2 (+158 bps YoY) and standalone H1 margin is 8.6%; management expects Mahad to reach 80%+ utilisation in two to three quarters, which should narrow the gap to standalone, though raw material inflation and pricing pressure cap upside.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Mahad is at about 50-55% of installed capacity, so the existing plant ramps to 80%+ without new capacity, but no new plant, line or expansion phase has a date; Mahad is designed for future phases with no timeline.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 sales volume is up 10% YoY at Baroda and 11% at Bareilly, Mahad sales volume rose 74% QoQ in Q2, and RFQs won in June are expected to go live from July to lift Q3 volumes.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at Baroda and Bareilly is not disclosed, and management said capex plans (brownfield or greenfield) will be announced in coming quarters, but gave no timeline and the company is in a consolidation phase with no substantial capex in 1-1.5 years.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance of Rs 1,000 crore turnover and Rs 50 crore PAT was confirmed, not raised; H1 PAT is Rs 8.3 crore, so the second half must deliver about Rs 42 crore, and pricing pressure makes an upgrade hard to see.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 PAT of Rs 8.3 crore leaves about Rs 42 crore needed in H2 to meet the Rs 50 crore FY27 target, and Mahad utilisation and camphor volume recovery are both unproven; the company has not revised guidance yet.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management said R&D is being strengthened for new molecules and Mahad is designed for additional molecules, but no specific product or launch date was named.

rows.label: RFQs won in June go live from July
rows.why: Management expects RFQs won in June to go live from July and lift volumes in Q3 FY27, with Q2 sales volume already up 12% QoQ at Baroda and 74% QoQ at Mahad.

rows.label: Unilever technical and manufacturing arrangement
rows.why: Management called it a work in progress, declined to share economics, did not say whether it involves investment or advances, and gave no timelines, so it is an unquantified upside at best.

rows.label: Working capital pressure lifts leverage
rows.why: Net debt-to-equity rose to 0.64 from 0.56 on higher inventory, receivables and input prices, which weighs on cash flow until the inventory and receivables unwind.

tone.note: Management was confident about record revenue, the 10-12% sales CAGR and the Mahad ramp to 80%+ utilisation, but was evasive on Unilever economics, capex timing and Mahad EBITDA break-even; analysts pressed on the 10% margin target, capex and the rise in net debt-to-equity to 0.64.
